facts.fact_text: Starting from 2010, a number of opposition parties or groups organised several demonstrations in Baku.
One of the unauthorised demonstrations in Baku took place on 19 June 2010.
One of the unauthorised demonstrations in Baku took place on 2 April 2011.
Opposition demonstrations in Azerbaijan were held on 2 April 2011.
The organisers of the demonstration of 2 April 2011 gave notice to the Baku City Executive Authority on 18 March 2011.
The aim of the demonstration of 2 April 2011 was, in particular, to demand the Government guarantee the right to freedom of assembly.
The aim of the demonstration of 2 April 2011 was, in particular, to demand the Government carry out democratic reforms.
The aim of the demonstration of 2 April 2011 was, in particular, to demand the Government release political prisoners.
The applicants decided to participate in the demonstration of 2 April 2011.
The applicant in application no. 56317/11 was arrested during the dispersal of the demonstration of 19 June 2010.
On 19 June 2010 the Sabail District Court convicted the applicant in application no. 56317/11 under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Sabail District Court sentenced the applicant in application no. 56317/11 to a fine of 20 Azerbaijani manats (approximately 20 euros).
The police dispersed the demonstration of 2 April 2011 by arresting demonstrators and forcing them into police vehicles and buses.
The applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 were arrested during the dispersal of the demonstration of 2 April 2011.
Later on 2 April 2011, formal decisions were drawn up to detain the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 as suspects in criminal cases.

On 4 April 2011 the prosecution formally charged the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 with a criminal offence under Article 233 of the Criminal Code (organisation of or active participation in actions causing a breach of public order).
By a judgment of 3 October 2011, the Sabail District Court convicted the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 under Article 233 of the Criminal Code.

The Sabail District Court sentenced the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 to various terms of imprisonment ranging from two years to two years and six months (as set out in the Appendix).
Some of the applicants in applications nos. 6814/13, 6903/13, 7990/13, 12717/13 and 28563/13 were arrested during the dispersal of the demonstration on 2 April 2011.
Some of the applicants in applications nos. 6814/13, 6903/13, 7990/13, 12717/13 and 28563/13 were arrested a few days after the demonstration of 2 April 2011.
By a judgment of 25 August 2011, the Sabail District Court convicted the applicants in applications nos. 6814/13, 6903/13, 7990/13, 12717/13 and 28563/13 under Article 233 of the Criminal Code.

The Sabail District Court sentenced the applicants in applications nos. 6814/13, 6903/13, 7990/13, 12717/13 and 28563/13 to various terms of imprisonment ranging from one year and six months to three years (as set out in the Appendix).
Mr Ulvu Guliyev (applicant in application no. 23365/14) was arrested on 8 April 2011.
Mr Rufat Hajibeyli (applicant in application no. 25680/14) was arrested on 22 April 2011.
The Nasimi District Court convicted the applicants in applications nos. 23365/14 and 25680/14 under Article 233 of the Criminal Code in its judgment of 10 October 2011.
The Nasimi District Court sentenced Mr Ulvu Guliyev (application no. 23365/14) to a term of imprisonment of three years.

The administrative-offence report stated that the applicant in application no. 56317/11 had committed an administrative offence under Article 310.1 (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer) of the Code of Administrative Offences.

On 4 April 2011 the prosecution formally charged the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 with a criminal offence under Article 233 of the Criminal Code (organisation of or active participation in actions causing a breach of public order).

On 9 April 2011 the prosecution formally charged Mr Ulvu Guliyev (applicant in application no. 23365/14) with a criminal offence under Article 233 of the Criminal Code (organisation or active participation in actions causing a breach of public order).

On 9 April 2011 the prosecution formally charged Mr Ulvu Guliyev (applicant in application no. 23365/14) with a criminal offence under Article 315.1 of the Criminal Code (resistance to or violence against a public officer).

On 23 April 2011 the prosecution formally charged Mr Rufat Hajibeyli (applicant in application no. 25680/14) with a criminal offence under Article 233 of the Criminal Code (organisation or active participation in actions causing a breach of public order).

Article 186.1 of the Criminal Code of Azerbaijan provides that deliberate destruction or damage of another's property which caused significant harm is punishable by a fine in the amount of 500 to 1,000 Azerbaijani manats, or deprivation of liberty for a period of up to two years.

Article 233 of the Criminal Code of Azerbaijan provides that organisation by a group of individuals of actions which grossly breach public order, or are associated with insubordination in respect of lawful demands of a public officer, or cause disruption of the normal functioning of transport, companies, public bodies and organisations, as well as active participation in such actions, is punishable by a fine in the amount of 5,000 to 8,000 Azerbaijani manats, or correctional labour for a period of up to two years, or deprivation of liberty for a period of up to three years.

Article 315.1 of the Criminal Code of Azerbaijan provides that use of violence against, or violent resistance to, a public officer in connection with the exercise of the latter's official duties, or use against the close relatives of such a public officer of violence which does not pose a danger to their life or health, or the threat of use of such violence, is punishable by deprivation of liberty for a period of up to three years.

The notice issued by the Baku city prosecutor's office on 1 April 2011 stated that if there was an attempt to hold a public assembly in places not agreed upon with the Baku City Executive Authority, illegal actions consisting of breach of public order and insubordination to lawful demands of public officers, or causing inconvenience to the population, or causing disruption of the normal functioning of transport, enterprises, bodies and organisations, would be prevented in accordance with the law.
The dispersal of the demonstration of 2 April 2011 resulted in isolated incidents of clashes between police officers and demonstrators.
It appears that several demonstrators at the demonstration of 2 April 2011 inflicted physical injuries on around twenty-five police officers.
It appears that several demonstrators at the demonstration of 2 April 2011 damaged two private vehicles.
It appears that several demonstrators at the demonstration of 2 April 2011 broke windows of some shops and offices located near the place where the demonstration was held.
The organisers of the demonstration of 2 April 2011 gave notice to the Baku City Executive Authority on 18 March 2011.
By a letter of 31 March 2011, the Baku City Executive Authority refused to authorise the holding of the demonstration of 2 April 2011 at the place indicated by the organisers.
The Baku City Executive Authority proposed by its letter of 31 March 2011 that the demonstration of 2 April 2011 be held at a different location from the one indicated by the organisers.

The organisers of the demonstration of 2 April 2011 decided to hold the demonstration in the central squares of Baku despite the Baku City Executive Authority's refusal to authorise the originally proposed location.

Video recordings submitted by some applicants show that on 2 April 2011, as soon as protesters began gathering in central streets of Baku, marching and chanting slogans calling for the government's resignation, the police started to disperse the demonstration.
The Sabail District Court found in its judgment of 3 October 2011 that the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 had disobeyed the orders of the police.

The Sabail District Court found in its judgment of 3 October 2011 that the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 had organised and actively participated in actions causing a breach of public order.

The Sabail District Court found in its judgment of 3 October 2011 that the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 had organised and actively participated in actions causing traffic jams.

The Sabail District Court found in its judgment of 3 October 2011 that the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 had organised and actively participated in actions causing destruction of private and public property.

The Sabail District Court found in its judgment of 3 October 2011 that the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 had organised and actively participated in actions causing infliction of injuries to twenty-five civilians and police officers.

In finding the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 guilty, the Sabail District Court relied on statements of civil claimants who testified that some unidentified participants in the demonstration had inflicted on them either physical or material damage.

In finding the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 guilty, the Sabail District Court relied on statements of police officers who testified that the applicants had actively participated in the demonstration, behaved aggressively, led other participants, chanted slogans and refused to obey orders of the police.

In finding the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 guilty, the Sabail District Court relied on a video recording which showed other participants in the demonstration of 2 April 2011 kicking and damaging a bus.
The Sabail District Court found in its judgment of 25 August 2011 that the applicants in applications nos. 6814/13, 6903/13, 7990/13, 12717/13 and 28563/13 had disobeyed the orders of the police.

The Sabail District Court found in its judgment of 25 August 2011 that the applicants in applications nos. 6814/13, 6903/13, 7990/13, 12717/13 and 28563/13 had actively participated in actions causing a breach of public order.

The Sabail District Court found in its judgment of 25 August 2011 that the applicants in applications nos. 6814/13, 6903/13, 7990/13, 12717/13 and 28563/13 had actively participated in actions causing traffic jams.

The Sabail District Court found in its judgment of 25 August 2011 that the applicants in applications nos. 6814/13, 6903/13, 7990/13, 12717/13 and 28563/13 had actively participated in actions causing destruction of private and public property.

The Sabail District Court found in its judgment of 25 August 2011 that the applicants in applications nos. 6814/13, 6903/13, 7990/13, 12717/13 and 28563/13 had actively participated in actions causing infliction of injuries to twenty-five civilians and police officers.

In finding the applicants in applications nos. 6814/13, 6903/13, 7990/13, 12717/13 and 28563/13 guilty, the Sabail District Court relied on the testimony of S.M., according to whom some protesters had hit his bus and damaged it.

In finding the applicants in applications nos. 6814/13, 6903/13, 7990/13, 12717/13 and 28563/13 guilty, the Sabail District Court relied on statements of police officers who testified that unidentified participants had behaved aggressively, chanted slogans and refused to obey orders of the police to disperse.

In finding the applicants in applications nos. 6814/13, 6903/13, 7990/13, 12717/13 and 28563/13 guilty, the Sabail District Court relied on testimonies of bystanders, according to whom unidentified demonstrators chanted slogans and disobeyed the police.
